description: Description Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is seeking a contract Business Systems Analyst to provide high-level analytical and technical support to the HR Systems & Automation organization. This role will partner with HR leaders, subject matter experts, Department of Energy (DOE) staff, Office of Personnel Management (OPM) representatives, IT teams, project teams, service providers, and other stakeholders. The analyst will implement, support, configure, integrate, and enhance Workday and other HR business applications. Key activities include fit-gap analysis, requirements gathering, solution design, functional specification development, configuration, data conversion, report and dashboard development, testing, documentation, training, and production support. Serving as a primary point of contact for assigned projects and operational activities, the analyst will translate business needs into scalable solutions, support continuous improvement, and help ensure HR systems are effective, reliable, secure, and aligned with BPA and DOE objectives. Key Responsibilities Provide business analysis expertise to design solutions and deliver data in support of HR programs and systems. Configure and support Workday solutions, including business processes, security, integrations, reporting, and analytics. Collaborate on the Workday product vision and multiyear roadmap, aligning priorities with BPA, DOE Human Capital, and IT objectives. Evaluate Workday modules not currently in use and recommend opportunities for future implementation. Support the full integration lifecycle, including discovery, requirements gathering, design, deployment, maintenance, and retirement. Develop custom reports, dashboards, analytics, and data solutions that support operations and enable informed decision-making. Conduct fit-gap, business process, and alternatives analyses while documenting recommendations and proposed solutions. Facilitate requirements, design, and improvement sessions with managers, SMEs, customers, service providers, and technical teams. Translate complex business needs into clear functional requirements, product requirements, configuration specifications, and implementation documentation. Evaluate vendor enhancements, regulatory changes, and system issues, working with vendors and stakeholders to define, document, and resolve impacts. Create and maintain functional specifications, design documents, job aids, user guides, standard operating procedures, and training materials. Develop, manage, and execute test plans, test scenarios, and test cases covering functional, regression, integration, and system-upgrade testing. Job Title: Business Analyst Job Description The Experienced Business Analyst plays a key role in documenting, refining, and maturing business processes for the Arctic and Offshore Patrol Ship and Joint Support Ship In-Service Support (AJISS) program. This role focuses on developing and renewing Value Stream Maps using LEAN methodologies, identifying areas for process improvement, and preparing Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) that clearly articulate benefits, value propositions, and financial impacts. The Business Analyst formulates compelling value propositions through detailed requirements specifications, presentations, and analysis of gaps, pain points, and opportunities for innovation. This position also collaborates closely with the AJISS team and Change Manager to adapt existing processes to align with updated information technology solutions and to foster a culture of collaboration and innovation across the enterprise. Responsibilities Lead the Business Analysis team within the AJISS program, ensuring clear process definition, documentation, and continuous maturity. Collaborate on the definition and refinement of business processes based on end‑user interviews, workshops, and pain points gathered from stakeholders within AJISS and within DND/RCN. Apply LEAN methodologies, including Value Stream Mapping, to assess enterprise process maturity and identify opportunities for improvement. Formulate clear and compelling value propositions in preparation for engagements with sponsors and customers, ensuring alignment with strategic objectives. Gather, analyze, and document detailed business and system requirements based on workshops and feedback from AJISS stakeholders and customers. Liaise with the broader AJISS team to ensure consistent and coherent messaging to the AJISS customer regarding process changes and improvements. Contribute to the development of Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs) using the approved AJISS template, including comprehensive descriptions of proposed changes, associated benefits, cost breakdowns, and overall value propositions. Identify and document gaps, pain points, and opportunities for innovation within existing processes and recommend practical solutions. Work with the AJISS Change Manager and IT stakeholders to adapt and optimize existing processes for integration with updated information technology offerings. Recommend strategies to promote a collaborative, innovative culture within DND/RCN and across the AJISS enterprise. Minimum of 5 years of demonstrated experience within the last 10 years leading business analysis activities or workshops in a large‑scale project environment. Actalent is currently seeking a qualified Business Systems Analyst for a position in Vancouver, WA. This Business Systems Analyst assignment is in the Transmission Technology System Development and Support (JDD) organization. This position performs systems analysis, interfacing with users to support functional requirements development, analysis of tools and serves as the primary liaison between Transmission Technology business units and the development team. Leads the elicitation, analysis, documentation, and validation of business and functional requirements for new and existing Operational Technology (OT) systems. Translate complex business needs into detailed technical specifications and user stories for system development and enhancement projects.. RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE: Work associated with this position will be directly related to business process support for systems change management, process and compliance requirements for the organization. Analyze system infrastructures, functional requirements, and technical capabilities for system acquisitions. Develop or review specifications, verifying that all essential requirements are documented. Distribute requirements to hardware and software configuration items or manual operations using appropriate modeling techniques including automated structured analysis tools. Review the logical top-level design for applications and information systems (including test plans and procedures). Verify that project software specifications, interface requirement specifications and software development plans are correct and of adequate scope. Review and validate that configuration management policies and procedures provide thorough requirements traceability through version release and adequate documentation to support system operation and maintenance. Code, test, install, and document detailed programs while applying applicable standards to all products. Prepare and conduct program presentations, in-house and client training, and functional education. Develop and present recommendations and support analysis for management decisions. Plan/recommend project operations’ schedules. Provide recommendations to BPA management for staffing requirements and resource allocations for projects. Prepare technical reports, documents, studies, and system documentation as required. Develop technical system concepts and designs to support proposal development and position papers. Attend meetings, conferences, and seminars to support the customer needs. Attendance also assists in maintaining currency of technical, procedural and acquisition knowledge. Monitor system performance to determine whether adjustments need to be made, and to determine where changes will need to be made in the future. Confer with system users to document and solve existing system problems. Communicate with management and co-workers by telephone, written form, e-mail, or in person. Support organizations change process and configuration management efforts

Job Title: Configuration Analyst 2 Job Description The Configuration Analyst 2 supports the Configuration and Data Management (CDM) group within the Deployables Operating Unit, performing essential configuration management and document control functions. This role focuses on planning, coordinating, and maintaining accurate project documentation, engineering changes, and product data to ensure that contract, engineering, and manufacturing requirements are consistently met. Responsibilities Plan and coordinate the preparation of project documentation, including engineering drawings, production specifications, schedules, and contract modifications to ensure customer contract requirements are fully met. Review contracts to determine the documentation required for each phase of the project, applying knowledge of engineering and manufacturing processes to define clear documentation needs. Analyze proposed changes to product design to determine their impact on the overall product and system, and communicate findings to relevant stakeholders. Coordinate modification records to maintain effective management control over configuration changes and ensure accurate tracking of all change activities. Establish change orders and prepare change authorization and documentation packages for internal teams and subcontractors, ensuring proper approvals and traceability. Review and analyze released engineering change data and ensure changes are correctly implemented and documented across affected products and systems. Coordinate engineering changes with engineering, quality, support, manufacturing, and engineering data control activities to maintain alignment and configuration integrity. Support and administer change management processes such as ECR, ECO, CR, and CI or similar workflows to control and document product changes. Manage and maintain bills of materials (BOMs), ensuring that product structures are accurate, current, and aligned with engineering and production requirements. Read and interpret engineering drawings, BOMs, and specifications to validate documentation and ensure correct implementation of product changes. Prepare reports, documentation, and status updates using Microsoft Office tools to communicate configuration status and change activities to project teams. Collaborate effectively with engineering, manufacturing, and program teams to resolve configuration issues and support smooth product lifecycle transitions. Essential Skills Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, Information Systems, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Minimum of 2 years of experience in configuration management, document control, product lifecycle management, or a similar discipline. Working understanding of configuration management principles and practices, including baselines, change control, configuration identification, status accounting, and audits. Experience supporting or administering change management process

Job Title: Geospatial Analyst / GIS Technician Job Description This Geospatial Analyst / GIS Technician role focuses on mining and managing geospatial data, maintaining large and complex file structures, and performing geometric corrections and orthorectification to ensure high-quality spatial data products. The position supports meaningful national security, intelligence, and defense missions, with daily work contributing to real-world operational outcomes and influencing critical decision-making. Responsibilities Conduct geospatial data mining to identify, extract, and organize relevant spatial information from multiple sources. Manage large geospatial file structures, ensuring data is well-organized, properly documented, and easily accessible for analysis and production. Perform geometric fixes on geospatial datasets to correct spatial inaccuracies and improve positional accuracy. Execute orthorectification tasks to produce accurate, georeferenced imagery suitable for analysis and operational use. Utilize ArcGIS and related geospatial tools to process, analyze, and visualize geospatial data. Apply strong computer skills to handle complex datasets, troubleshoot technical issues, and optimize workflows. Support geospatial and GEOINT missions that contribute to national security, intelligence, and defense objectives. Collaborate with analysts and technologists to ensure geospatial products meet operational requirements and support real-world outcomes. Maintain data integrity and quality control throughout the geospatial processing lifecycle. Essential Skills Proficiency with ArcGIS and related geospatial software tools. Experience performing orthorectification and geometric corrections on geospatial data and imagery. Strong computer skills, including working with large datasets and complex file structures. Background in geography or a related field, ideally supported by a geography degree. Ability to manage and organize large geospatial data repositories effectively. Capacity to support mission-focused geospatial work tied to national security, intelligence, and defense. Additional Skills & Qualifications Geography degree or equivalent education in geospatial sciences, GIS, or a closely related discipline. Interest in supporting GEOINT missions and contributing to real-world operational outcomes. Ability to work independently in a remote or hybrid environment while maintaining high standards of quality and productivity. Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy and integrity. Work Environment The role offers a flexible work environment with options for 100% remote, hybrid, or onsite work, based on candidate preference. The standard work schedule is Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, with the option to work a 4x10 schedule consisting of four 10-hour days. Candidates must reside in Colorado, with a preference for those located in Northern Colorado or the Denver metro area. For any onsite or client-facing activities, the dre

Quality Operations Analyst I Schedule: Monday-Friday | Full-Time Work Arrangement: Hybrid Overview We are seeking a motivated Quality Operations Analyst I to support quality systems, master data governance, and quality operations within a regulated manufacturing environment. This role is ideal for early-career professionals looking to build expertise in quality systems, data management, compliance, and operational excellence within the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or medical device industries. The Quality Operations Analyst will play a key role in maintaining quality-related data across enterprise platforms, supporting quality notifications and investigations, ensuring data integrity, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to drive compliance and operational efficiency. This position offers exposure to industry-leading systems including SAP QM, Teamcenter, MES, and LIMS while providing valuable experience in quality operations and manufacturing support. Key Responsibilities Maintain quality-related master data and records across SAP, Teamcenter, MES, LIMS, and related systems. Process and support quality notifications, including NCRs, RMAs, RTVs, and investigation activities. Perform data validation, correction, remediation, and governance activities to ensure system accuracy and compliance. Troubleshoot SAP Quality Management (QM) transactional issues impacting manufacturing and quality operations. Your job is to build a Perplexity-enabled solution that reads completed SOW content and automatically pre-populates Life of Study budget inputs — and vice versa — so that our managers and directors are refining a data-informed baseline rather than starting effort estimations from scratch every time. We have approximately 30 existing SOWs and years of historical Life of Study budgets across our active study portfolio that you will use as training examples to build and test the solution. The solution also needs to generate cost saving recommendations and flag items requiring closer review for budgeting accuracy — including areas where effort may be under-budgeted, over-budgeted, incomplete, or inconsistent with study assumptions. This is a solo individual contributor role. There is no project manager. You own the work end to end from requirements gathering through solution development, proof of concept, implementation, and knowledge transfer What You Will Do: Review and deeply understand both the SOW workbook and the Life of Study budget workbook — their structure, data fields, logic, and how information flows between them Define how Perplexity will be used to interpret and normalize SOW content into recommended Life of Study budget inputs including rules, prompts, exception handling, and required human review points Build data mapping and business rules that connect SOW services, assumptions, units of work, estimated hours, and direct cost logic to Life of Study budget stages, effort allocation structures, and budget categories Develop and test a prototype or minimum viable solution demonstrating how SOW information is translated into draft Life of Study budget inputs for user review and refinement Build a review and exception framework that highlights recommended checkpoints for accuracy, missing information, unusual effort patterns, and potential under or over budgeting Generate cost saving recommendations by analyzing how SOW services and assumptions drive Life of Study budget costs and identifying areas where effort or direct costs may be reduced with minimal impact to study quality Test the solution using representative study scenarios and refine it for robustness, consistency, and operational usability Manag
